userStories.title: Parse the handoff body and bounded record shape
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the stable handoff input parser and share existing top-level flow validation without changing spec-form behavior.

**Motivation** — The record lives in `.nax/features/<feature>/workflow/<runId>/` (`result.json`, `ledger.md`), which is git-excluded, so it must travel with the request.

**Approach** — `POST /api/fleet/flows` (the existing nax-entry create) accepts a second body form. A body carries either `features` (the existing spec form, unchanged) or `handoff` (this form), never both. `remoteUrl`, `branch`, `roles` and `costCapUsd` stay top-level, exactly as in the spec form:
```json
{
  "remoteUrl": "https://github.com/acme/widgets",
  "branch": "feat/chat-layout-overflow",
  "roles": { "reviewer": "acp:claude", "supervisor": "acp:claude" },
  "costCapUsd": "5",
  "handoff": {
    "feature": "chat-layout-overflow",
    "headSha": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
    "record": [
      { "runId": "8bd38595-ffbf-4092-89d0-f1ebbf375786", "file": "result.json", "mtimeMs": 1763370000000, "content": "{...}" },
      { "runId": "8bd38595-ffbf-4092-89d0-f1ebbf375786", "file": "ledger.md", "mtimeMs": 1763370000000, "content": "..." }
    ]
  }
}
```
- `record` holds every run directory of the feature's `workflow/` folder that has a `result.json`: earlier runs carry story records and ledger items that `--publish-only` still reads (`collectStoryRecords`, `collectLedgerItems` walk every run directory, newest first by `result.json` mtime).
- `file` is `result.json` or `ledger.md`. `content` is the file's UTF-8 text. `mtimeMs` is the file's mtime on the sender's machine, an integer from 0 to `8640000000000000` (the Date range `utimes` accepts); the runner restores it, so nax's newest-first order is the sender's order.
- `headSha` is 40 lowercase hex characters.
- `remoteUrl`, `branch`, `roles` and `costCapUsd` follow exactly the rules `parseFlowInput` applies to the spec form. The implementation extracts those checks from `flow-input.ts` into one shared helper both parsers call.

`NormalizedHandoffFlowInput` keeps the input's shape: `{ remoteUrl, branch, roles, costCapUsd, handoff: { feature, headSha, record } }`. `parseFlowHandoffInput` is therefore idempotent: parsing its own output returns an equal object. This is what lets the approval command re-parse the stored body, as the spec form does today.

Limits. The values live in `packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts` (the runner imports them). The API image does not ship that package at runtime (it imports it type-only, see `apps/api/src/fleet/common/protocol.spec.ts`), so `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-handoff-input.ts` keeps its own copies and a spec pins them equal to the protocol's:
- `HANDOFF_MAX_RUNS = 20` distinct run ids.
- `HANDOFF_RECORD_MAX_BYTES = 524288`: the sum of the UTF-8 byte lengths of every `content`. Fastify's default 1 MiB body limit applies (no `bodyLimit` override); a body over it is refused with 413 before the handler, which the nax sender avoids by enforcing the same content cap.
- `HANDOFF_RUN_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/` (a path segment; nax run ids are UUIDs). Two entries whose run ids are equal ignoring case and whose `file` is the same are duplicates, and two run ids equal ignoring case but spelled differently are refused, because a macOS runner's filesystem folds case.
- `HANDOFF_RECORD_FILES = ['result.json', 'ledger.md']`.

Parser errors are `ValidationAppException({ reason }, 'fleet.flowInput')` naming the property, as `parseFlowInput` does.

**Scope** — In: new parser/type/limit copies, body-form exclusivity, entry/file/byte/run-count/mtime validation, shared top-level validation extracted into a reusable exported helper in the existing flow-input.ts, new co-located unit spec. Out: newest-run publishability and PRD reader (US-002), protocol exports/pinning/persistence (US-003), endpoint/approval integration (US-004/005), runner parsing/restoration (US-007). Validating the record's truth beyond its shape and the newest run's publish preconditions, including any feature name recorded inside `result.json`; the record gets the same trust as the specs `nax-flow__send` sends today.

**Interface** — `parseFlowHandoffInput(body: unknown): NormalizedHandoffFlowInput`; `NormalizedHandoffFlowInput` keeps `{ remoteUrl, branch, roles, costCapUsd, handoff: { feature, headSha, record } }`. US-002 extends this parser's content rules; a publishable record must already survive this story unchanged.

userStories.title: Validate the newest publishable run and read handoff PRDs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the handoff parser with newest-run publishability and expose nax-compatible PRD readiness reading.

**Motivation** — nax already has the mechanism: a run with `workflow.publish` set to `push` or `none` ends with outcome `pushed` or `local-only`, and `nax run -f <feature> --publish-only` publishes it later from its record when the record's `head` equals HEAD and no PRD story is pending (nax `packages/nax/src/workflow/publish-only.ts`, `packages/nax/src/cli/publish-only-refusal.ts`).

**Approach** — The **newest run** is the run whose `result.json` entry has the largest `mtimeMs`; two `result.json` entries with the same largest `mtimeMs` are refused, so "newest" is never ambiguous. Its `result.json` parses as a JSON object with `schemaVersion: 1` and a `featureWorkflow` object whose `step` is `"done"`, whose `outcome` is `"pushed"` or `"local-only"`, and whose `head` equals `handoff.headSha`. These are `publishOnlyStart`'s own preconditions.

`record` holds every run directory of the feature's `workflow/` folder that has a `result.json`: earlier runs carry story records and ledger items that `--publish-only` still reads (`collectStoryRecords`, `collectLedgerItems` walk every run directory, newest first by `result.json` mtime).

In `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-handoff-input.ts`: `parseFlowHandoffInput(body: unknown): NormalizedHandoffFlowInput`, the type `NormalizedHandoffFlowInput`, the four limit copies, and `readHandoffPrd(text: string): { branchName: string | null; pendingStoryIds: string[] } | null` (null when the text is not a JSON object with a `userStories` array). A story is pending by nax's own rule (`isPendingStory`, nax `packages/nax/src/prd/index.ts`): `passes` is not true and `status` is none of `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `blocked`, `paused`, `regression-failed`, `decomposed`. Parser errors are `ValidationAppException({ reason }, 'fleet.flowInput')` naming the property, as `parseFlowInput` does.

A run id with ledger.md but no result.json is refused with reason handoff.record. Only the newest run's content is checked for publishability; older draft records remain available for ledger/story collection. Preserve normalized shape, order and idempotence established in US-001.

**Scope** — In: content validation and PRD reader in the upstream parser and its existing unit spec. Out: shape/shared-validator work already delivered by US-001, persistence/protocol (US-003), forge fetches and HTTP error mapping (US-004/005), runner execution (US-007). Validating the record's truth beyond its shape and the newest run's publish preconditions, including any feature name recorded inside `result.json`; the record gets the same trust as the specs `nax-flow__send` sends today.

**Interface** — `parseFlowHandoffInput(body: unknown): NormalizedHandoffFlowInput`; `readHandoffPrd(text: string): { branchName: string | null; pendingStoryIds: string[] } | null`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a run id that has a ledger.md entry but no result.json entry throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with two result.json entries sharing the largest mtimeMs throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run result.json whose content is not valid JSON throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run result.json whose schemaVersion is 2 throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run featureWorkflow.step of publish throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run featureWorkflow.outcome of draft throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run featureWorkflow.head different from handoff.headSha throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.

[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with an older run whose result.json has outcome draft and a newer run (larger mtimeMs) with outcome local-only returns a normalized input, because only the newest run is checked.

[unit] readHandoffPrd called with a PRD whose branchName is feat/x and whose stories are one { status: 'passed' }, one { status: 'failed' } and one { status: 'pending', passes: false } with id US-003 returns { branchName: 'feat/x', pendingStoryIds: ['US-003'] }.
[unit] readHandoffPrd called with a PRD that has no branchName returns an object whose branchName is null.
[unit] readHandoffPrd called with the text not json returns null.

[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run result.json that is not a JSON object, lacks schemaVersion: 1 or lacks a featureWorkflow object throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.
[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with a newest-run featureWorkflow.outcome of ready throws ValidationAppException with reason handoff.record.

[unit] parseFlowHandoffInput called with its normalized output for a publishable pushed handoff returns a deep-equal object after newest-run validation is added, preserving US-001's approval-replay idempotence.

suggestedCriteria: readHandoffPrd returns no pendingStoryIds for stories with passes:true regardless of their status.
readHandoffPrd returns no pendingStoryIds for passed, failed, skipped, blocked, paused, regression-failed and decomposed stories when passes is not true.
readHandoffPrd returns null for a JSON array or an object without a userStories array.
parseFlowHandoffInput accepts tied older result.json mtimes when the largest result.json mtime is unique.

userStories.title: Persist handoff records and extend the assignment protocol
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add additive storage and protocol contracts while keeping large records out of ordinary flow reads and approval details.

**Motivation** — The record lives in `.nax/features/<feature>/workflow/<runId>/` (`result.json`, `ledger.md`), which is git-excluded, so it must travel with the request.

**Approach** — Storage:
- `FleetFlowFeature` gains `handoff Boolean @default(false)` and `handoffRecord Json?`. Every flow read the repository returns (`create`, `findById`, `lockById`, `findPage`, `findLiveForThread`, `findLiveForSpec`, `findLiveForBranch`) loads features with `omit: { handoffRecord: true }` (Prisma 7.10 supports `omit` without a preview flag), and `toFeature` / `toDomain` are typed against the omitted row. So the record is never re-read on every advance tick and never reaches `FleetFlowFeatureDto.from` or the approval details, and `expect(await repo.findById(id)).toEqual(created)` keeps holding.
- A new repository method `IFleetFlowRepository.findHandoffRecord(featureId): Promise<HandoffRecordFile[] | null>` reads the record for the RUN dispatch only.
- `FleetFlowFeatureRecord` gains an optional `handoff?: boolean` (the repository always sets it). `CreateFleetFlow` gains an optional `handoff?: { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }` that the repository writes onto the flow's first feature (`handoff: true`, `handoffRecord: record`). `CreateFlowInput.handoff` is the single carrier from the route to the repository; feature inputs never carry the record.
- `FleetJob` gains `handoff Json?`. `FleetJobRecord` and `NewFleetJob` (`jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts`) gain an optional `handoff?: HandoffRecordFile[] | null`, typed with the protocol's `HandoffRecordFile` (no import from `flows/` into `jobs/`). `createJob` (`jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts`) writes it as `Prisma.InputJsonValue`, and `Prisma.DbNull` when absent, as it writes `agentInput`; `toJob` maps it back.
- The record is stored on the approval request input, the flow feature and the RUN job, and sent once in the ASSIGN payload: at most four copies of at most 512 KiB, accepted. The approval request's stored `input` is readable to whoever can read that approval, the same exposure as any create body.

`AssignPayload` (`packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts`). Target: gains `handoff?: HandoffAssign` with `HandoffAssign = { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }` and `HandoffRecordFile = { runId: string; file: 'result.json' | 'ledger.md'; mtimeMs: number; content: string }`, plus the four limit constants.

Limits. The values live in `packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts` (the runner imports them). The API image does not ship that package at runtime (it imports it type-only, see `apps/api/src/fleet/common/protocol.spec.ts`), so `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-handoff-input.ts` keeps its own copies and a spec pins them equal to the protocol's:
- `HANDOFF_MAX_RUNS = 20` distinct run ids.
- `HANDOFF_RECORD_MAX_BYTES = 524288`: the sum of the UTF-8 byte lengths of every `content`. Fastify's default 1 MiB body limit applies (no `bodyLimit` override); a body over it is refused with 413 before the handler, which the nax sender avoids by enforcing the same content cap.
- `HANDOFF_RUN_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/` (a path segment; nax run ids are UUIDs). Two entries whose run ids are equal ignoring case and whose `file` is the same are duplicates, and two run ids equal ignoring case but spelled differently are refused, because a macOS runner's filesystem folds case.
- `HANDOFF_RECORD_FILES = ['result.json', 'ledger.md']`.

`FleetFlowStartCommand.details` (`fleet-flow-start.command.ts`). Baseline: returns `features: flow.features`. Target: returns each feature mapped explicitly to `{ feature, specPath, dependsOn, handoff }`.

Add `IFleetFlowRepository.findLiveForBranch(repoId, branch)` with the existing live-state definition, independent of specSha. Ship the three columns in one migration and regenerate the Prisma client. Extend existing repository integration specs, protocol.spec.ts for parity and fleet-flow-start.command.spec.ts for projected details; the invariant is that approval details never carry handoffRecord.

**Scope** — In: protocol exports, schema/migration, repository/domain mapping, lazy record lookup, branch lookup and approval-detail projection. Out: CreateFlowInput/service carrier and branch-busy use (US-004), route/approval variant (US-004/005), RUN decision/dispatch/payload emission (US-006), runner implementation (US-007). Clearing the stored record from the flow feature, the job or the approval request after the flow ends.

**Interface** — `IFleetFlowRepository.findHandoffRecord(featureId): Promise<HandoffRecordFile[] | null>`; `IFleetFlowRepository.findLiveForBranch(repoId, branch)`; `handoff?: boolean`; `handoff?: { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }`; `handoff?: HandoffRecordFile[] | null`; `HandoffAssign = { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }`; `HandoffRecordFile = { runId: string; file: 'result.json' | 'ledger.md'; mtimeMs: number; content: string }`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] The API copies of HANDOFF_MAX_RUNS, HANDOFF_RECORD_MAX_BYTES, HANDOFF_RUN_ID_RE and HANDOFF_RECORD_FILES in flow-handoff-input.ts equal the constants exported by @nathapp/fleet-protocol.

[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findById on a flow created with handoff: { record } returns a first feature whose handoff is true.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findById on a flow created with handoff: { record } returns a first feature that has no handoffRecord key.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.create with handoff: { record } returns a flow whose first feature has no handoffRecord key.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findById on a flow created without handoff returns features whose handoff is false.

[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findLiveForBranch(repoId, branch) returns the RUNNING flow on that repo and branch even when its specSha differs from a caller's previously held specSha; only repoId and branch are passed to the method.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findLiveForBranch(repoId, branch) returns null when the only flow on that repo and branch is COMPLETED.
[integration] The job repository's createJob with handoff set to a record, followed by findById, returns a job whose handoff equals the record.
[integration] The job repository's createJob without handoff, followed by findById, returns a job whose handoff is null.
[unit] FleetFlowStartCommand.details for a request on a handoff flow returns features whose first entry equals { feature, specPath, dependsOn: [], handoff: true }.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findHandoffRecord(featureId) returns null when featureId does not exist.

[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findById returns a flow deep-equal to the value returned by create for the same handoff flow, preserving the existing create/read equality despite the omitted record.

routing.reasoning: Cross-package protocol and additive database migration spanning flow/job repositories, omitted-row typing and approval-detail data projection; no access-control changes.

suggestedCriteria: PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findPage, lockById, findLiveForThread, findLiveForSpec and findLiveForBranch return features without handoffRecord keys.
FleetFlowStartCommand.details returns no handoffRecord key even when the supplied repository fixture contains one.
PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findHandoffRecord returns null for a non-handoff feature or missing feature.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `details` assertion may pin `features` as the repository's feature objects; `details` now maps each feature to `{ feature, specPath, dependsOn, handoff }`, so the expectation becomes that mapped shape, and the invariant is that the approval details never carry `handoffRecord`.

userStories.title: Create approval-gated GitHub handoff flows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept the handoff form on the existing NAX create route, verify GitHub state and persist a pending flow under branch-wide exclusion.

**Motivation** — The owner ruled (2026-11-17) that the chain hands the feature over **before** publishing (approach A) and uploads its run record with the request (transport T1).

**Approach** — `FleetFlowsController.create` (`fleet-flows.controller.ts`). Baseline: parses with `parseFlowInput(body, 'NAX')`, checks the spec files at `specSha`, and maps `RepoCheckException` inline in its `catch`. Target: the inline mapping is extracted into one private method both forms call unchanged; when the body has a `handoff` key the route parses with `parseFlowHandoffInput(body)`, runs the handoff checks below, then opens the route gate with the variant `NAX_HANDOFF_FLOW_CREATE_VARIANT` and `input: { projectId, repoId, body: <normalized> }`; a body without `handoff` keeps the baseline path exactly.

Create checks for the handoff form (in order):
1. Body parse (`parseFlowHandoffInput`): 400 `fleet.flowInput` naming the property.
2. Repo resolution, project reach and `fleet.flow.create` permission: exactly as the spec form today.
3. `branch` equal to the repo's `defaultBranch`: 400 `fleet.flowInput` reason `branch`.
4. Forge reads with one read credential (GitHub: `mintThreadReadToken`; GitLab: the `read` credential):
   - branch head differs from `handoff.headSha`: 409 `fleet.flows.handoffHeadMoved`;
   - `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json` absent at the head, or not readable by `readHandoffPrd`: 422 `fleet.flows.prdMissing` with `{ path }`;
   - that PRD's `branchName` is null or differs from `branch`: 422 `fleet.flows.handoffBranchMismatch` (the runner checks out `prd.branchName`, so a mismatch would publish a different branch than the flow guards);
   - a pending story in that PRD: 422 `fleet.flows.handoffStoriesPending` with `{ storyIds }`;
   - an open PR from the same repository (GitHub `headRepoFullName` equal to the repo's `owner/name`; GitLab merge requests listed for the project) whose `headSha` equals `handoff.headSha`: 409 `fleet.flows.handoffPrOpen` with `{ prNumber }`. The listing reads one page of 100.
   - A forge failure maps through the extracted mapping exactly as the spec form maps it (`forgeUnavailable` 503, `repoNotConnected`, `gitlabNotConnected`, `branchNotFound`). Every read fails closed: no flow is created.
5. Route gate with `NAX_HANDOFF_FLOW_CREATE_VARIANT`, then `FleetFlowsService.create` with `entry: 'NAX'`, `specSha: headSha`, one feature `{ feature, specPath: '.nax/features/<feature>/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }`, `handoff: { record }`, and the live-branch refusal `fleet.flows.branchBusy`.

The flow is created `PENDING` with the `fleet.flow.start` ask, as every nax-entry flow is; nothing billed starts before approval. New API i18n keys (`apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}`): `fleet.flows.handoffHeadMoved`, `fleet.flows.prdMissing`, `fleet.flows.handoffBranchMismatch`, `fleet.flows.handoffStoriesPending`, `fleet.flows.handoffPrOpen`, `fleet.flows.branchBusy`.

`GitHubAppClient.mintThreadReadToken` (contents, pull_requests and metadata read), `.getBranchHead`, `.getFile`, `.listOpenPullRequests` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts`; `OpenPullRequest` carries `number`, `headSha` and `headRepoFullName`, and the listing reads one page of 100). `mintReadOnlyToken` cannot list pull requests, so the handoff form never uses it.

`CreateFlowInput` (`fleet-flows.service.ts`). Target: gains `handoff?: { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }`.

`FleetFlowsService.lockNaxEntry`. Baseline: refuses a live flow on `(repoId, branch, specSha)` with `fleet.flows.duplicate`. Target: for a handoff, refuses a live flow on `(repoId, branch)` whatever its sha, with `ConflictAppException({ flowId }, 'fleet.flows.branchBusy')`, through a new repository method `IFleetFlowRepository.findLiveForBranch(repoId, branch)`.

Pass the single CreateFlowInput.handoff carrier into repository creation; feature inputs never carry the record. This story also registers `NAX_HANDOFF_FLOW_CREATE_VARIANT = 'rest:fleet-nax-handoff-flow.create'` in `FlowRouteCommands.onModuleInit` (`flow-route.commands.ts`): its `parse` runs `parseFlowHandoffInput` on the stored `body` (the normalized object) and its `run` calls `FleetFlowsService.create` with `entry: 'NAX'`, `specSha: body.handoff.headSha` and `handoff: { record: body.handoff.record }`. The endpoint acceptance criteria run through that real registered command, never a fake gate. Extend endpoint coverage using real persistence and stubbed forge reads.

**Scope** — In: handoff branch routing, shared forge-error mapping, GitHub checks, service carrier/branch refusal and six bilingual keys. Out: GitLab handoff implementation, registered approval command and OpenAPI regeneration (US-005), storage internals (US-003), RUN dispatch (US-006). Adopting a draft PR that was already published from chat by another account; this feature refuses that case with `fleet.flows.handoffPrOpen`. A handoff from a fork or for a repository other than the registered `FleetRepo`. Open-PR detection beyond the first page of 100 open PRs on GitHub, and telling apart two branches that share the same head commit.

**Interface** — `CreateFlowInput.handoff?: { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }`; `NAX_HANDOFF_FLOW_CREATE_VARIANT = 'rest:fleet-nax-handoff-flow.create'`; gate input `{ projectId, repoId, body: <normalized> }`; `ConflictAppException({ flowId }, 'fleet.flows.branchBusy')`.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] POST /api/fleet/flows with a valid handoff body for a GitHub repo, where the stubbed forge reports the branch head equal to headSha, a prd.json at the head whose branchName equals branch with no pending story, and no open PR, stores a flow whose { state, entry, specSha } equals { state: 'PENDING', entry: 'NAX', specSha: headSha }.

[integration] The flow stored by that valid GitHub handoff create has one feature equal on { feature, specPath, dependsOn, handoff } to { feature: handoff.feature, specPath: '.nax/features/<feature>/spec.md', dependsOn: [], handoff: true }.
[integration] The valid GitHub handoff create mints its GitHub token with GitHubAppClient.mintThreadReadToken and never calls mintReadOnlyToken.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete the handoff create path for GitLab and approval replay, and document the handoff form in the create-body API contract.

**Motivation** — The owner ruled (2026-11-17) that the chain hands the feature over **before** publishing (approach A) and uploads its run record with the request (transport T1).

**Approach** — `FlowRouteCommands.onModuleInit` (`flow-route.commands.ts`): US-004 registers; this story pins with its acceptance criteria `NAX_HANDOFF_FLOW_CREATE_VARIANT = 'rest:fleet-nax-handoff-flow.create'`, whose `parse` runs `parseFlowHandoffInput` on the stored `body` (the normalized object) and whose `run` calls `FleetFlowsService.create` with `entry: 'NAX'`, `specSha: body.handoff.headSha` and `handoff: { record: body.handoff.record }`.

Create checks for the handoff form (in order):
1. Body parse (`parseFlowHandoffInput`): 400 `fleet.flowInput` naming the property.
2. Repo resolution, project reach and `fleet.flow.create` permission: exactly as the spec form today.
3. `branch` equal to the repo's `defaultBranch`: 400 `fleet.flowInput` reason `branch`.
4. Forge reads with one read credential (GitHub: `mintThreadReadToken`; GitLab: the `read` credential):
   - branch head differs from `handoff.headSha`: 409 `fleet.flows.handoffHeadMoved`;
   - `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json` absent at the head, or not readable by `readHandoffPrd`: 422 `fleet.flows.prdMissing` with `{ path }`;
   - that PRD's `branchName` is null or differs from `branch`: 422 `fleet.flows.handoffBranchMismatch` (the runner checks out `prd.branchName`, so a mismatch would publish a different branch than the flow guards);
   - a pending story in that PRD: 422 `fleet.flows.handoffStoriesPending` with `{ storyIds }`;

   - A forge failure maps through the extracted mapping exactly as the spec form maps it (`forgeUnavailable` 503, `repoNotConnected`, `gitlabNotConnected`, `branchNotFound`). Every read fails closed: no flow is created.
5. Route gate with `NAX_HANDOFF_FLOW_CREATE_VARIANT`, then `FleetFlowsService.create` with `entry: 'NAX'`, `specSha: headSha`, one feature `{ feature, specPath: '.nax/features/<feature>/spec.md', dependsOn: [] }`, `handoff: { record }`, and the live-branch refusal `fleet.flows.branchBusy`.

userStories.title: Start handoff flows at RUN and transport the record to assignment
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Dispatch and recover a handoff feature's initial publish-only RUN while preserving all post-RUN flow decisions.

**Motivation** — A chat chain that runs a feature ends with a draft PR held by open items, and koda cannot finish it: nax trusts only item-index and item-thread comments its own login wrote (`ownComments`, nax `packages/nax/src/forge/marker.ts`), so a PR the owner's account published can never be readied by koda's bot (`no nax item index on this PR`).

**Approach** — Steps:
A handoff feature skips SPEC_REVIEW, PLAN and PRD_REVIEW:
- No job yet, flow `APPROVED` or `RUNNING`: dispatch `RUN`.
- A handoff flow never dispatches `SPEC_REVIEW`.
- An `APPROVED` handoff flow whose `RUN` job exists (queued at or after `approvedAt`) is recovered to `RUNNING` at step `RUN` by the advance pass, as an adopted `SPEC_REVIEW` is today.
- Every later decision is the existing one: a finished RUN with `prNumber` and `resultSha` dispatches `REVIEW`, then `RULE` / `FIX` / complete / `WAITING_ANSWER` per #413, with one automatic RULE/FIX round. A RUN that fails stops with `step_failed`; a RUN that ends without a PR stops with `run_no_pr`.

`FlowStepInput` and `decideFlowStep` (`flow-step-decision.ts`). Target: input gains an optional `handoff?: boolean` (absent means false; `decisionInput` sets it from the feature); see Steps below.

`BuildStepDispatchInput` and `buildStepDispatch` (`flow-step-dispatch.ts`). Baseline: `RUN` takes its ref from the PLAN job's `resultBranch` and throws without a PLAN. Target: input gains `handoff?: boolean`; a handoff `RUN` uses `ref: flow.specSha` (the head sha) and needs no PLAN.

`FleetFlowAdvanceService` (`fleet-flow-advance.service.ts`). Target: the dispatch pass of a handoff `RUN` reads the record with `findHandoffRecord`; a null record stops the flow with reason `dispatch_refused` and detail `RUN: handoff record missing` instead of dispatching; a record is passed as `handoff` in the `FleetJobsService.dispatch` options. For every other dispatch the `handoff` key is **omitted** from the options object (never `undefined` or `null`), so the existing exact-options assertions keep passing. The crash-recovery rule (`recoverable`, near line 657) also covers a handoff feature's `RUN` job queued at or after `approvedAt`, exactly as it covers an adopted `SPEC_REVIEW`.

`FleetJobsService.dispatch(actorId, projectId, dto, opts)` (`jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts`). Target: `opts` gains `handoff?: HandoffRecordFile[]`, stored on `FleetJob.handoff` only for `command: 'RUN'`. `DispatchFleetJobDto` does **not** gain the field: only a flow can dispatch a handoff RUN.

`buildAssignPayload` (`jobs/assign-payload.ts`). Target: a RUN job with a non-null `handoff` adds `handoff: { record }` to the payload; every other command never does.

Use the feature.handoff domain flag from US-003, its lazy findHandoffRecord and job persistence. Preserve dispatch claim, parent/flow lock order, job insert/record split, creator access and budget guards; lookup the record only for handoff RUN dispatch rather than on every tick. Keep RUN job links atomic so recovery uses the existing job rather than creating a second billed RUN. Existing exact-options tests should continue to require absence of handoff for all non-handoff dispatches. Retain ordinary failure details and ingest wait behavior; nax's refusal text remains in RUN logs. Extend the existing decision, dispatch, advance integration and assignment specs as part of implementation.

**Scope** — In: initial step choice, SHA ref, lazy record dispatch/refusal, crash recovery, RUN-only job storage and assignment emission. Out: create/parser/provider/approval paths (US-001/002/004/005), schema/repository/protocol declarations (US-003), runner restoration/argv/profile/result handling (US-007). A handoff field on DispatchFleetJobDto or any public job-dispatch route is excluded. Changing REVIEW/RULE/FIX, adding a capability gate or surfacing nax refusal text in stop details is excluded.

**Interface** — `FlowStepInput.handoff?: boolean`; `BuildStepDispatchInput.handoff?: boolean`; `FleetJobsService.dispatch(actorId, projectId, dto, opts)` with `opts.handoff?: HandoffRecordFile[]`; RUN assignment `handoff: { record }`.

userStories.title: Restore handoff records and publish on the runner
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make RUN assignments carrying handoff restore prior workflow files and invoke publish-only without misattributing those files as this job's result.

**Motivation** — The record lives in `.nax/features/<feature>/workflow/<runId>/` (`result.json`, `ledger.md`), which is git-excluded, so it must travel with the request.

**Approach** — Runner:
For a RUN assign with `handoff`, `HostExecutor`:
1. checks out as for every RUN (`prepareCheckout` reads `prd.json` at the ref, which is the head sha, and checks out `prd.branchName`; a leftover local branch ahead of origin can make HEAD differ from the head sha, which `--publish-only` then refuses);
2. calls `restoreHandoffRecord(repoDir, feature, handoff.record)` before nax starts;
3. writes the job profile with `publishPr: true`;
4. spawns `buildNaxArgv`, which appends `--publish-only`;
5. reads the workflow result and stashes the workflow outputs with `excludeRunIds = handoffRunIds(assign)`, so the restored `result.json` (which qualifies by mtime when the sender's clock runs ahead of the job's creation time) is never mistaken for the publish's own result.

`parseAssign` (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts`). Target: validates and keeps `handoff` on a RUN with the protocol's limits and the same entry rules as the API; `bad('handoff')` for a malformed block or a non-RUN command carrying one.

`buildNaxArgv` (`apps/runner/src/executor/nax-process.ts`). Baseline RUN argv: `[...naxCommand, 'run', '--headless', '--json', '-f', feature, '--profile', chain, '--max-cost', cap]`. Target: a RUN assign with `handoff` appends `'--publish-only'`.

`jobProfileContent` and `writeJobProfile` (`apps/runner/src/executor/job-profile.ts`). Target: both gain a new **last** optional positional parameter `publishPr?: boolean`; when true the profile includes `workflow: { publish: 'pr' }`. The job profile deep-merges after the repo config, so the PR is published whatever the repo's `workflow.publish` says.

`findWorkflowResult(featureDir, sinceMs)` (`apps/runner/src/verdict/workflow-result.ts`). Target: gains an optional third parameter `excludeRunIds?: ReadonlySet<string>`; a run directory whose name is in it is never returned, even when its `result.json` mtime is at or after `sinceMs`.

`stashWorkflowOutputs` (`apps/runner/src/executor/workflow-stash.ts`). Target: gains an optional `excludeRunIds?: ReadonlySet<string>` passed through to `findWorkflowResult`.

`HostExecutor.readWorkflowResult` and `HostExecutor.collectBundle` (`apps/runner/src/executor/host-executor.ts`). Target: for a RUN assign with `handoff`, both pass `handoffRunIds(job.assign)` as `excludeRunIds` (derived from the persisted assign, never from memory, so a daemon restart cannot lose them).

In `apps/runner/src/executor/handoff-restore.ts`: `restoreHandoffRecord(repoDir: string, feature: string, record: readonly HandoffRecordFile[]): Promise<void>`, which removes `featureDirFor(repoDir, feature)/workflow` entirely (the runner's `clean -ffd` keeps git-ignored files, so earlier jobs' run directories survive in the clone), writes each file to `workflow/<runId>/<file>`, and sets each file's atime and mtime to `mtimeMs`; and `handoffRunIds(assign: AssignPayload): ReadonlySet<string>`, the distinct run ids of `assign.handoff.record`, empty when there is no handoff.

Limits imported from protocol: `HANDOFF_MAX_RUNS = 20` distinct run ids; `HANDOFF_RECORD_MAX_BYTES = 524288` summed UTF-8 content bytes; `HANDOFF_RUN_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$/`; `HANDOFF_RECORD_FILES = ['result.json', 'ledger.md']`. `mtimeMs` is an integer from 0 to `8640000000000000`. Two entries whose run ids are equal ignoring case and whose file is the same are duplicates; run IDs equal ignoring case but spelled differently are refused. Record must be nonempty, entries must have string content and allowlisted files, and every represented run needs result.json. Revalidate assignment entry shape/limits before any filesystem use; API owns newest-run content preconditions and nax owns final HEAD/content refusal. For parseAssign tests, put the described payload inside a FleetCommandOut ASSIGN envelope with matching jobId; the function accepts the envelope, not a bare payload. The existing command-handler.ts rejection branch must continue returning before supervisor.begin for malformed handoffs. Use featureDirFor and the protocol's run-id segment contract, not the shorter generic assertSegment limit.

Preserve all non-handoff RUN behavior and all PLAN, REVIEW, FIX, AGENT, THREAD and config behavior. Add the last profile parameter without shifting existing context/model/relay/cost arguments. Apply publish overlay to raw and relay profiles. Exclusion must flow through result reading and workflow stashing on both ordinary execution and readoption. Extend existing parser, argv, profile, result and stash specs; use temporary real files and utimes for restoration and injected git/nax spawn for HostExecutor tests, never the installed nax or host credentials.

**Scope** — In: runner parse/retain validation, regression verification of the existing command-handler assignment rejection path, restore helper and unit spec, argv/profile overlay, workflow result/stash exclusions and HostExecutor wiring. Out: API shape/publishability/PRD rules (US-001/002), protocol definitions/storage (US-003), create/approvals/providers (US-004/005), flow dispatch/payload producer (US-006). Do not implement the nax chat/send half, change own-login trust, add a runner capability gate, clear server-side record storage or surface nax refusal logs as flow stop detail.

**Interface** — `restoreHandoffRecord(repoDir: string, feature: string, record: readonly HandoffRecordFile[]): Promise<void>`; `handoffRunIds(assign: AssignPayload): ReadonlySet<string>`; last positional parameter `publishPr?: boolean` on `jobProfileContent` / `writeJobProfile`; optional `excludeRunIds?: ReadonlySet<string>` on `findWorkflowResult` (third) and `stashWorkflowOutputs` (last); assignment `handoff?: HandoffAssign` where `HandoffAssign = { record: HandoffRecordFile[] }` and `HandoffRecordFile = { runId: string; file: 'result.json' | 'ledger.md'; mtimeMs: number; content: string }`.
